title: undeclared-transitive-trust-crosses-boundary

proposition.statement: A relying system must not infer that trust, recognition, accreditation, or authority is transitive across another actor or registry boundary unless a competent rule explicitly permits that transitivity for the relevant scope.

preconditions: Actor or authority A recognises B for a stated scope.
B recognises C for some scope or proposition.
No competent rule has established that A's recognition of B extends transitively to C for the relying decision.

trigger.statement: The relying system treats A-to-B and B-to-C relationships as sufficient authority for an A-to-C trust conclusion.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence of the declared relationships among the actors or authorities in the chain.
Evidence establishing the authority and scope of each actor that participates in the recognition chain.
Evidence of any competent rule that permits, constrains, or prohibits transitive recognition for the relevant scope.
Evidence showing how separate recognition relationships are being composed into the relying conclusion.

falsification.condition: The system returns PASS for an A-to-C trust conclusion solely because A recognises B and B recognises C without an applicable transitivity rule.
The system treats an undeclared transitivity policy as permissive rather than unresolved or prohibited.

references.note: Repository judgment record for the composition failure tranche.
